steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage (UC inflamed vs control)
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. The counts come from Salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, so the import state is not established. Fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, and do not invent a length input (R-0169@18ab).

With 6 replicates per group, DESeq2 flags a gene with a count outlier by Cook's distance and sets its p-value to NA; report the number of such genes and inspect the counts of any flagged gene that matters to the question (R-0039@968d).
The size factors account for the depth difference of sample_01; a depth difference alone is not a reason to drop it (R-0030@2248).

plan.title: UC colon hallmark pathway activity per sample
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is gene-level counts from Salmon for 12 human colon samples (6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch; 12,000 genes), with sample_01 at roughly a quarter of the median library size. The question asks for a pathway activity score per sample, a heatmap of hallmark activity across samples, and the pathways that separate treated from control. The plan therefore (1) runs sample-structure QC on blind variance-stabilized counts to see how the conditions and the low-depth sample behave before any test, (2) fits the standard two-group count model (DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage) to obtain the gene-level contrast, a full ranked gene list, and the normalized expression for scoring, (3) computes a per-sample activity score for every MSigDB Hallmark set with GSVA on the log-normalized matrix — the method of choice here because the deliverable is a matrix of many gene sets across a fixed sample set that a limma model tests — and tests each set's scores between UC-inflamed and control, (4) renders the hallmark-by-sample heatmap annotated by condition and summarizes which hallmark pathways separate the groups, (5) corroborates at the gene level with a preranked fgsea pass against the same Hallmark collection on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and (6) compiles a reproducible report. The Salmon gene-level table carries no per-sample quantification or transcript-length table, so the count model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and that limitation is stated in the report.

GSVA per-sample pathway scores on vst log-normalized expression, then limma on the score matrix with the design and BH across signatures
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark
structured report with method, package versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, sessionInfo, seed and collection versions

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
